purpose: Keep frequent changes and discarded experiments inexpensive over the product lifetime; make major changes explicit and controlled while preserving owner data.
priority_order: Preserve owner intent and trustworthy evidence.
Make changes local, observable, testable and reversible where possible.
Keep the amount of context needed for a change bounded.
Deliver useful desktop behavior with a small operational footprint.
Optimize scale only against measured constraints.

cheap_by_priority: Replace a provider or supported parser
controlled_cost: Rewrite a module or product language
change_cost_policy.abstraction_rule: Add a boundary for a concrete trust/dependency boundary or observed change pressure. Expected savings must justify the code, tests and compatibility burden; universal cheap change is not a requirement.
change_cost_policy.experiment_rule: Record the question, bounded scope, success/failure evidence and retirement condition in the ordinary change record. Keep experimental output disposable unless explicitly adopted; remove unsuccessful or retired implementations.
change_cost_policy.measurement: Review recurring cross-owner edits, time spent recovering failed experiments and migration burden. Set targets from actual work; do not substitute interface counts or arbitrary file quotas for change cost.

shape.style: Local-first modular monolith; explicit ports at actual external dependencies; feature-oriented code inside each module.
shape.default_processes: One desktop host with background jobs. Use a separate collector only across a real OS boundary or for measured isolation needs.
shape.deployment: Installed desktop application; no browser UI or mandatory cloud backend.
shape.extension_rule: Add a typed seam for an observed replacement or trust boundary; do not make every class an interface.
shape.module_rule: A module is a cohesive responsibility and data owner, not a separate service. Split or merge boundaries when change evidence warrants it.

owns: Retained source identity anchors and pinned evidence
Referenced interpretation identity anchors and mappings

forbidden_responsibilities: Executing deployments as a side effect of reading status

owns: Future external execution and telemetry integrations
forbidden_responsibilities: Cross-module table writes outside owner-specific repositories
Business persistence outside application use cases

dependency_semantics.direction: A -> B means A may compile against B's published contracts; never B's internals.
dependency_semantics.granularity: Catalog edges are upper bounds. Concrete project references must be narrower. Each adapter depends only on the ports it implements.
dependency_semantics.internal_visibility: Hide implementation types. Use project/namespace checks to enforce contract-only references; do not publish all types merely for test convenience.
dependency_semantics.composition: Only hosts choose concrete adapters. Modules and application never reference adapter implementations.
dependency_semantics.features: Within a module group code by use case, with local implementation details. Avoid repository-wide Controllers/Services/Models directories.
dependency_semantics.shared_types: Share identity primitives only. Map boundary DTOs deliberately; do not pass mutable domain entities or a universal graph object everywhere.
dependency_semantics.cross_module_work: Application invokes typed owner operations in explicit order. Use typed read contracts for queries; no implicit event chains for ordinary use cases.
dependency_semantics.ui_boundary: Application returns presentation-neutral response DTOs using its own contracts and Foundation values; do not leak module entities, database records or provider DTOs into Desktop.
dependency_semantics.package_count: Do not generate one project per catalog entry automatically. Introduce contract assemblies where needed to enforce the chosen dependency rules.

classes.meaning: What a source or analyzer reported at a specific snapshot; observations remain bounded by coverage and tool limitations.
Replaceable, evidence-linked explanations or hypotheses; never silently promoted to observations.
Owner ideas, corrections, alternatives and decisions; revisions survive analysis replacement.
Revisioned proposals and work derived from a chosen desired state; priority changes preserve history.
Recorded result for an explicit criterion revision, subject snapshot and environment; not a blanket completion assertion.

data_model.identity: RepositoryId is independent of root path; EntityRef combines repository and stable ID. Paths and labels are attributes, not primary identities.
data_model.rename: Preserve identity when evidenced; retain old-to-new mappings and flag ambiguous matches. Do not move owner notes to guessed targets silently.

identity_lifecycle.rule: Allocate source identity independently of path and retain minimal anchors/mappings while referenced by owner records; disposable source indexes do not own those anchors.

Allocate repository-scoped hypothesis IDs independently of graph layout or model-generated labels. Retain the original anchor and analysis revision when an owner record references it; AttachIdea coordinates this retention with Intent.
Allocate owner-defined identities without requiring an observed source entity; subsequent source links are revisioned associations.

data_model.reinterpretation_identity: Reuse an interpretation ID only with supported continuity. Record split/merge candidates as mappings; ambiguous or one-to-many changes retain the original historical reference and remain unresolved until an owner selects a revisioned association. Never fan out or reassign notes silently.
data_model.idea_attachment: Application.AttachIdea uses one unit of work to retain the target anchor through Evidence.RetainSourceAnchor or Understanding.RetainEntityAnchor and record the revisioned association through Intent.CaptureIdea. Intent stores the reference without importing those modules; a failed attachment leaves no dangling owner association.
data_model.cross_repository: Each end of a link carries its own RepositoryId, SnapshotId and freshness. No claim of an atomic global repository snapshot.
data_model.boundary_rule: Typed records are authoritative. Graph nodes, layouts, search indexes and status cards are projections; changing their presentation does not redefine domain identity.
data_model.criteria: Planning owns criterion definitions and immutable revision/hash. Verification receives a value copy plus reference/hash, and records results independently; no reverse dependency on Planning.
data_model.historical_evidence: A reference alone is not a retained copy. Pin the permitted excerpts/artifacts needed by adopted decisions and verification; expose missing/expired source evidence explicitly.
data_model.privacy_and_retention: Retention and user-directed deletion override audit retention. If evidence is deliberately purged, retain only permitted metadata and mark dependent claims unverifiable; never promise indefinite recoverability.

steps: AdoptExplanation names a command ID, exact analysis revision, selected entity references and expected owner revision. Return an existing result for an identical completed command; reject command-ID reuse with a different payload. Validate evidence references, scope, retention permission and input availability without rerunning a model.
Prepare, hash and finalize permitted retained artifacts outside the database write transaction using the storage artifact protocol.

Within one application unit of work, recheck revisions and permissions, invoke Evidence.PinEvidence, Understanding.RetainAnalysis and Intent.AdoptDecision, and record command completion plus any dependent job intent.
Return the committed decision and retained output revisions. Retrying the same command cannot create duplicate adoption records.
evidence_backed_adoption.failure: A conflict, missing required input or denied retention aborts all canonical adoption changes. Finalized unreferenced files may remain for garbage collection; they do not imply adoption succeeded.
evidence_backed_adoption.limits: This flow is for adopting evidence-backed analysis. User-authored ideas or decisions may be recorded independently without fabricated provenance; later permitted deletion marks affected claims unverifiable. Semantic evidence support requires reviewed behavior evaluations in addition to reference validation.

storage.choice: SQLite for local canonical records, plus versioned artifact files for large data where needed.
storage.canonical: Owner-authored intent, decisions, accepted plans, verification history, referenced entity anchors and identity mappings, pinned evidence, adopted analysis outputs, configuration references and jobs.
storage.derived: Unadopted analysis, source indexes, dependency projections, search caches and graph layouts may be rebuilt or regenerated.
storage.ai_reproducibility: Regenerating an AI result is not deterministic replay. Preserve the exact adopted output and its lineage instead of relying on rerunning a model.
storage.ownership: One host is the canonical writer. Modules own table namespaces and migrations; owner-specific persistence adapters use shared transaction infrastructure.
storage.change_ownership: The affected data owner defines record semantics, compatibility and migration. Adapters implement engine/serialization mechanics; Application coordinates multi-owner transactions. Read only affected stores and consumers unless a shared engine change demonstrates wider impact.
storage.atomicity: Commit canonical owner state, revision/audit record and dependent job intent in one local transaction where required. A composite operation uses the application unit of work and owner APIs, not foreign table writes.
storage.artifact_commit: Write new artifacts to temporary files, hash and atomically finalize them, then commit the canonical reference. Protect pending artifacts from garbage collection until the transaction outcome is known; reconcile interrupted writes on restart. Coordinate pin/deletion changes through the owning APIs. Garbage-collect unreferenced files; never assume a filesystem rename and SQL commit are one atomic operation.
storage.cache_loss: After a cache loss, rebuild projections from canonical records and available source snapshots; mark unavailable historical input instead of reconstructing imaginary facts.
storage.concurrency: Expected-revision checks protect owner edits; serialized short write transactions avoid holding database locks during scanning or AI calls.
storage.backup: Use consistent SQLite backup facilities and a manifest for referenced retained artifacts; verify hashes and restore into a fresh profile. Do not copy an active database file alone.
storage.export: Offer versioned implementation-independent JSON records plus retained artifact manifest, with stable IDs and explicit schema versions. Export is for portability; it is not a second live source of truth.
storage.migration: Prefer additive changes, backfill and compatibility readers. Record minimum reader/writer versions. Refuse an incompatible older writer; back up before destructive migration.
storage.schema_rollback: Rollback code only when the stored schema remains compatible. Otherwise use a tested forward fix or restore with explicit accounting for post-backup edits.
storage.wsl_rule: Keep the database on the writer host's local filesystem. A WSL collector never opens the Windows database through a mounted/network path.

steps: A file/Git event marks the selected repository dirty; periodic/startup reconciliation covers missed events.
Collect immutable permitted input and create a snapshot with content identity and coverage. Detect files changing during collection and retry or mark the capture partial.
Publish deterministic supported observations atomically for that snapshot.
Build structural projections; show supported facts while semantic interpretation remains pending.
Schedule bounded AI interpretation only for affected input; validate output before storing it as interpreted data.
Overlay selected owner scenario and current planning/verification views without rewriting underlying observations.
refresh_pipeline.snapshot_definition: Commit identity alone is insufficient: include worktree changes, selected untracked content, exclusions and analyzer input hashes. Do not claim a moving live directory is an atomic snapshot.
refresh_pipeline.invalidation: Track artifact-to-input dependencies; if impact is uncertain, invalidate the affected repository projection rather than silently retaining it as current.
refresh_pipeline.publication: Use run/snapshot and expected-current-generation checks. Old results can remain historical, but cannot overwrite a newer projection.
refresh_pipeline.view_consistency: Expose structural and semantic generations separately. A composite response names its source snapshots and pending/partial/stale components.
refresh_pipeline.job_semantics: Persist intent and completion state. Assume at-least-once scheduling with idempotent publication; do not claim exactly-once external requests.
refresh_pipeline.restart: Recover interrupted jobs, reconcile repository state and retry only operations known to be safe. External requests with unknown outcome require reconciliation.
refresh_pipeline.limits: Bound queue size, worker concurrency, input size and retries; coalesce obsolete refresh work; keep user actions responsive.
refresh_pipeline.diagnostics: Correlate commands, snapshots, runs and artifact IDs; keep structured local logs with content/secret redaction and bounded retention.

roles.fast: Local explanations, simple evidence-grounded questions and idea structuring.
roles.deep: Cross-module impact, alternative designs, disputed interpretations and planning.

ai_boundary.selection: Roles are capability profiles, not fixed providers or model counts. One model may serve both; map roles after representative evaluations.
ai_boundary.context: Retrieve relevant evidence and owner decisions through read contracts. Both roles may inspect original evidence; a fast summary is not the sole deep-model input.
ai_boundary.routing: Use task type, scope, uncertainty and failed validation; bound escalation. High-impact recommendations require deeper evidence review regardless of fast-model confidence.
ai_boundary.output: Require versioned typed output, existing evidence references, scope and uncertainty. Reject unknown references or incompatible schemas; do not persist malformed output as facts.
ai_boundary.authority: Models propose; deterministic application code enforces permissions, budgets, revisions and adoption. Model text cannot grant tool or execution authority.
ai_boundary.budget: Reserve estimated usage before concurrent dispatch, reconcile actual usage and block new paid jobs when limits are reached. Surface unknown cost where the provider cannot report it.
ai_boundary.offline: Existing maps and owner records remain usable without AI. New semantic work is visibly pending/unavailable; do not fabricate fallback answers.
ai_boundary.security: Send only permitted evidence; source text is untrusted data. Secrets are referenced through the host secret store and never stored in prompts, logs or project exports.
ai_boundary.provider_failure: Do not silently send code to a different provider. Fallback providers require an established data/permission policy.

process_boundary.when: Introduce a collector process for confirmed Windows/WSL placement, parser isolation or measured responsiveness needs; otherwise use in-process adapters.
process_boundary.transport: Prefer host-launched child processes with framed versioned messages over private stdio for the local/WSL case. No public listener by default.
process_boundary.boundary: Validate roots, message sizes and schemas on both sides; frame stdout exclusively for protocol, stderr for redacted diagnostics. Never interpolate repository paths into shell command text.
process_boundary.ownership: Collector returns observations/artifacts and has no canonical database or owner-decision write access. The host validates and publishes them.
process_boundary.disconnect: Timeout/cancel explicitly; retain last known state as stale and reconnect with reconciliation. Protocol version mismatch yields actionable diagnostics, not silent data loss.

execution_extension.separation: A future executor is a separate adapter/process consuming an explicit work specification; it is not a privilege of the analysis model.
execution_extension.change_flow: Use an isolated checkout when appropriate; return a patch and verification evidence. Integrate through the established authority policy.
execution_extension.irreversibility: Remote deployments, payments and messages cannot be undone by changing a local revision. Reconcile outcomes and use operation-specific compensation or owner decisions.
execution_extension.audit: Keep execution request, permission decision, tool outcomes and subject revisions separate from inferred task status.

quality_attributes.replaceability: A renderer or provider replacement passes unchanged boundary acceptance fixtures without altering canonical intent records.
quality_attributes.locality: A private implementation change touches its owner and tests. Cross-boundary changes declare affected contracts and consumers; do not enforce arbitrary file-count quotas.
quality_attributes.recoverability: Demonstrate fresh-profile restore, cache rebuild, interrupted job recovery and incompatible-version rejection.
quality_attributes.freshness: Choose measured structural/semantic refresh budgets after reference repository and hardware selection; always show age and coverage even when a target is missed.
quality_attributes.performance: Keep IO/AI/layout work off the UI thread; virtualize focused graphs. Choose benchmarks before accepting the graph renderer, not after adding full product scope.
quality_attributes.maintainability: Track recurring cross-module changes and contract churn. Revise a poor boundary rather than adding workarounds indefinitely.
